content.title: About
content.content: Cherry strudel is a classic baked dessert made from thin pastry dough filled with a sweet cherry mixture. The dough is prepared from flour, eggs, butter and water, while the filling consists of fresh or frozen cherries, sugar and sometimes aromatic spices such as cinnamon and vanilla.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Strudel originates from Austria, where it is considered a national dish.
The cherry version became popular in Eastern Europe thanks to abundant cherry harvests.
Traditional strudel dough is rolled out to a thickness of 1–2 mm.
Original recipes often include nuts and raisins, but cherry strudel is frequently served without them.
Strudel is commonly dusted with powdered sugar or served with a butter sauce.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cherries contain anthocyanins and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the cherries and whole‑grain dough promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium in cherries helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When made with modest butter, the pastry contains less saturated fat than many other baked goods.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑wheat dough provides B1 and B3 vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough contains wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The filling is often sweetened, so those monitoring blood sugar should limit portion size.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Butter and dough make the strudel energy‑dense; moderation is key.

items.title: Acidity of cherries
items.content: For some individuals the tartness of cherries may cause heartburn.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the strudel warm, sliced into portions. It can be dusted with powdered sugar, drizzled with butter sauce, or paired with ice cream. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain dough and reduce added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the strudel in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven before serving to restore a crisp crust.
